components.name: sr25519 (Schnorrkel — Schnorr over Ristretto255), keystore surface

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha1 0.10.6 is a locked dependency of this substrate-api-client workspace. Its in-tree consumers are soketto 0.8.1 (Cargo.lock:5768) and tungstenite 0.28.0 (Cargo.lock:7152), both used for the RFC 6455 WebSocket handshake (Sec-WebSocket-Accept), where SHA-1 is protocol-mandated rather than a security digest. Available in the shipped library; no application call site found — replaceable only by the WS-transport vendors.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: k256 0.13.4 is the Rust secp256k1 implementation backing sp_core::ecdsa::Pair — the concrete curve behind the keystore's ecdsa_* functions (keystore/src/lib.rs:243-277) and the ecdsa_bls381 paired-key scheme. Presence is the fact here: secp256k1 ECDSA (and its recovery variant used by Substrate accounts) is Shor-vulnerable; replacement is decided by polkadot-sdk upstream.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA (secp256k1 via k256, cf. ALG-6e1f67ab) is the keystore's third account scheme alongside ed25519/sr25519. sp_core::ecdsa signs with secp256k1 and SHA-256 prehash (sign_prehashed takes a 32-byte prehashed message). Classical signature — Shor-vulnerable; migration ML-DSA-65, and upstream Substrate decides availability.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 capability behind sp-core/sp-io's ed25519 key type (sp-io depends on ed25519-dalek, Cargo.lock:6076); the ac-keystore exposes it through its ed25519_* methods (keystore/src/lib.rs:219-241, judged separately). Quantum-unsafe signature (Shor); migration ML-DSA-65. Changeable only with the Substrate/polkadot-sdk ecosystem, not in this repo alone.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The Curve25519/Ristretto255 group arithmetic backing ed25519-dalek (Ed25519) and schnorrkel (sr25519 signatures/VRF — schnorrkel depends on it, Cargo.lock:5445). Part of the shipped Substrate key stack; quantum-unsafe elliptic-curve group. Replaceable only by the polkadot-sdk ecosystem.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 is the TLS 1.3 key exchange of the DEFAULT RPC transport: jsonrpsee-client-transport 0.26 (Cargo.lock:2722) uses rustls 0.23.35 (Cargo.lock:5181) whose provider is ring 0.17.14 (ring has no ML-KEM, so no post-quantum group is offered). Traffic to a wss:// node endpoint is harvestable now and decryptable once a CRQC exists. Changeable here by switching the TLS stack (e.g. rustls with aws-lc-rs provider).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (substrate's KeccakHasher, the original Keccak padding rather than FIPS-202 SHA3-256) used as the message prehash when signing with ecdsa_bls381 paired keys. The hash itself is quantum-tolerant (Grover gives only a square-root speedup) — the A- rating stands; the signing chain it feeds is what is classical. Compiled only when substrate's bls_experimental feature is enabled.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 ships in the substrate hashing stack: a second sha2 0.10.9 is locked at Cargo.lock:5667 and pulled by sp-crypto-hashing (Cargo.lock:6001-6009) for sha2_256. Dep-level capability; no direct application call site found (app hashing goes through BlakeTwo256/Config::Hasher). Hashes are Grover-only risk — not urgent, CNSA 2.0 prefers 384-bit digests.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-GCM is the TLS record-layer AEAD of the default jsonrpsee TLS transport (rustls 0.23.35 + ring). Symmetric AE is not Shor-broken; the session secrecy rests on the X25519 KEX (ALG-defedad1). Recorded as the bulk-crypto half of the shipped TLS posture.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: rustls 0.23.35 is the TLS provider behind jsonrpsee's client-ws-transport-tls feature (root Cargo.toml:63), used by the default async JsonrpseeClient: WsTransportClientBuilder::default().build(url) at api-client/src/rpc/jsonrpsee_client/mod.rs:34-36. The lockfile pins rustls to the ring 0.17.14 provider (rustls deps: ring, rustls-webpki — Cargo.lock:5181-5191) with rustls-platform-verifier for roots. Consequence: TLS 1.3 with a classical X25519 key share only — rustls 0.23 can offer X25519MLKEM7

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.17.14 is the crypto provider for rustls and rustls-webpki in this build: TLS 1.3 ECDHE key exchange (X25519), AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD, SHA-2 digests, and webpki certificate signature verification (Ed25519, ECDSA P-256/P-384, RSA). ring 0.17 has no ML-KEM implementation, so its presence is what denies the rustls X25519MLKEM768 hybrid here. Available in the shipped library; the application reaches it via the jsonrpsee TLS transport.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same Cargo.lock entry as ALG-683d5cd2 (Ed25519 via ed25519-dalek 2.2.0): the crate and the algorithm object are one dependency asset under two names; linked so a reader references a single entry. Ed25519 is behind sp-core/sp-io for the keystore's ed25519_* methods.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OpenSSL bindings reach the build through native-tls (tungstenite's TLS feature, api-client/Cargo.toml:33) for the optional TungsteniteRpcClient. PQ capability is decided by the system OpenSSL linked at build time — the crate version does not decide it; with OpenSSL 3.5+ the X25519MLKEM768 hybrid is negotiated by default. Observable here, replaceable by the platform/vendor, not by editing this crate version.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same Cargo.lock entry as ALG-725ecd3e (SHA-1 via sha1 0.10.6): one dependency asset under two names; linked. Consumer is the WebSocket handshake where RFC 6455 mandates SHA-1 — replaceable only by the WS-transport vendors.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC's in-tree consumers: rfc6979 0.4.0 (deterministic ECDSA nonces for the k256/secp256k1 ECDSA stack, Cargo.lock:4989-4999) and substrate-bip39 (PBKDF2-HMAC for mnemonic→seed derivation, Cargo.lock:6624-6629) behind the keystore's Pair::from_string phrase path. HMAC-SHA256/512 is itself quantum-acceptable (Grover-only); recorded as the MAC layer of the shipped key-derivation and ECDSA stacks.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: native-tls is the TLS provider of the optional tungstenite transport (feature tungstenite-client, api-client/Cargo.toml:76). TLS version and KEX groups are delegated to the platform OpenSSL at runtime (openssl 0.10.78/openssl-sys in the lock); the repo pins no TLS configuration itself. PQ is achievable without code change by linking OpenSSL ≥3.5 (X25519MLKEM768 default) — observable here, replaceable by the platform.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha2 0.9.9 (SHA-256/SHA-512) — the older of two sha2 lines in the lockfile (a 0.10.x entry also exists at Cargo.lock:5667) — reached via the Substrate/sp-core dependency chain, feeding BIP39 seed derivation and Substrate hashing helpers. SHA-2 digests are quantum-tolerant (Grover square-root only); the 0.9.x line is just notable as an unmaintained major version, not a PQ issue.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same Cargo.lock entry as ALG-82f1eeb2 (Curve25519 via curve25519-dalek 4.1.3): one dependency asset under two names; linked. Provides the Ristretto255 group for sr25519/schnorrkel and the ed25519-dalek backend.
